entities.summary: Alfred Tennyson, 1st Baron Tennyson was an English poet. He was Poet Laureate of the United Kingdom during much of Queen Victoria's reign. In 1829 he was awarded the Chancellor's Gold Medal at Cambridge for one of his first pieces, "Timbuktu". He published his first solo collection of poems, Poems, Chiefly Lyrical, in 1830. "Claribel" and "Mariana", which remain some of Tennyson's most celebrated poems, were included in this volume. Although described by some critics as overly sentimental, his poems ultimately proved popular and brought Tennyson to the attention of well-known writers of the day, including Samuel Taylor Coleridge.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Tennyson's poetry played a significant role in shaping the literary landscape of Victorian England, influencing notable writers like Oscar Wilde and Robert Browning. His work also had a lasting impact on British culture, with his poems being studied and admired for generations.
